result:
My verdict is **PASS** for candidate `sha256:619d74ff…fdfac` (freeze commit `987ae02`): both assigned findings are fixed and verified as closed, but I raised one new Low finding.

**Candidate identity:** HEAD at start was `e77be1a`, not the freeze commit `987ae02`. It is a direct child that adds only candidate-excluded metadata (assignments, manifest, `stages.json`). The recomputed candidate ID matched in the real repo and in a full clone at `987ae02`, so I went ahead, as round 11 did. During my run HEAD moved to `163d0ca`, the domain reviewer's auto-commit. I looked only at its file names, and the ID did not change.

**Findings**
- **F-DG1-132 (Low): CLOSED_VERIFIED.** The fix is `792973b`, which adds rule 5 to `apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts:121, 299-355`. My probe flagged all 25 forms of binding the whole `node:crypto` module, including the 7 from the assignment, E1–E5 and 11 variants I added. `import { setEngine }` is still a rule-1 violation. The 4 allowed controls (named imports, the cookie and `Object.entries` patterns) stay clean. The real module tree has zero violations, and `architecture.test.ts` passes 122/122 on Node 22 and Node 24. I also checked at runtime that no other named export of an allowed built-in reaches `setEngine`, and none of the 14 allowed third-party dependencies does either.
- **F-DG1-133 (Low): CLOSED_VERIFIED.** The "not closable statically" wording and the "would break" citation are gone. Rule 5 is documented at :45-52, and residual (a) at :71-81 now covers only plain objects and third-party code, which matches what I measured. The "41 module files" wording is loose: 41 is the total number of module files, and only 5 of them import `node:crypto` (all with named imports).
- **F-DG1-134 (new; Low, not a mandatory violation, owner backend-workflow-engineer).** The module lint only scans `.ts`/`.tsx` files (`walk()` at `architecture.testkit.ts:167-172`).
  - **Reproduced:** a planted `modules/transformations/zzx.mts` gets zero violations, while the same source as `.ts` gets 2. It typechecks, builds and passes eslint, `dist/zzx.mjs` is produced, and loading it reaches `crypto.setEngine`. The plant also deep-imports `../access/policy.ts`, so it slips past the module boundary check as well.
  - **Age and current impact:** it dates back to the original DG1 commit `8332624`, and the current tree has no such files.
  - **Rating and fix:** I rated it Low, in line with earlier lint-bypass findings such as F-DG1-109. The fix is to scan every JS/TS file extension under `modules/` (or treat any other file there as a violation) and add a self-check for a planted `.mts` file.

**Checks** (in a throwaway clone, dependencies installed offline from a copy of the local package store)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| typecheck, build, lint, openapi:lint, no-cdn, format:check | all pass |
| Unit tests | 315/315 on Node 22 and on Node 24 |
| Integration (disposable PostgreSQL 16, port 5491) | 200/200 in each of two runs on Node 22, plus 200/200 on Node 24 |
| Gate and agent tooling tests | 105/105 |
| Deploy script tests | 59/59 |
| Install-sandbox suite | 13/14 |
| SBOM check | OK |
| DG0 historical validation | PASS |
| Three `ci.yml` copies | byte-identical; the CI dependency check passes |

**Checks not marked PASS**
- **AC-1 (effect) and a real-repo install: BLOCKED.** They need the package registry, and this sandbox has no network.
- **SEC-R12-02 (file-scope probe): FAIL.** This is the check that found F-DG1-134.

The gate validator rejects any gating review that has a check not marked PASS. As it stands, this record cannot be used for DG1 approval without orchestrator action. Round 11 had the same BLOCKED check.

**Requirements:** REQ-DLV-025, REQ-DLV-033, REQ-DLV-042, REQ-S16-001, REQ-S16-003, REQ-S16-004, REQ-S19-004 and REQ-S19-006 are all IMPLEMENTED with every evidence file present, and this round's own runs back them. No Critical, High or mandatory-violation finding is open.

The throwaway clone and scratch files are removed, nothing is left running on port 5491, and the candidate source is untouched.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-12/`:
- `code-security-reviewer.json`
- `code-security-reviewer.verifications.json`
- `code-security-reviewer.findings.json`
- `code-security-reviewer.md`

The record and the findings file pass the gate schemas, and all 68 evidence references exist. The evidence logs are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-12/`.
